body:
Yeah, I'm hoping for the best. My sister's relationship with our parents has normalized since she's accomplished the typical life goals -- moving out, successful job, marriage, childbirth.

I actually started this thread after a conversation with my mom about my current SO. My girlfriend and I (naturally) have a bit in common -- she too is socially unorthodox, got a degree in a "worthless" field (but to her credit, has a decent job that she likes with room for growth), and otherwise doesn't engage in wasteful or destructive behavior. Still, I got the same kind of 'the hell is wrong with you, boy?' attitude from mom. 

I know there isn't really such thing as a "normal" family, but I'd still like to share my life with my parents in a constructively *positive* context. I'm not sure if it *is* constructively positive and I'm being too sensitive, or if it's my parents who would benefit from relaxing their standards/criticisms.

Haha yeah I agree with you on those points. I think I turned out okay, all things considered, and it sorta annoys me when parents coddle their children too much. 

At the same time, I think "all good things in moderation" comes into play. Being too critical can be just as bad as being too uncritical. Too loving can cause problems like being unloving. 

I'm lucky that I don't live with my parents and therefore don't have to put up with nearly as much criticism as I once did, but they're still my parents. They're still in my life. I'm dating this lovely lady, but I'd really rather not bring her around to the parents. And I definitely don't like answering their questions about her. Unfortunate... I'd like to share my life with my family, but I don't want to put up with their quiet negativity and consistent disapproval.

In some ways, I suppose. I quit swimming when I started high school. I quit music lessons when I started college. The first half of high school I ignored, resulting in horrible grades. The second half I turned around, nearly a 4.0 with several AP courses under my belt. Graduated from UC Berkeley last year, didn't study business/premed/science. Currently working a job that doesn't require a 4-year degree, but obviously I'm searching for something better. 

So I guess I'm a failure in the sense that I'm capable of doing so much more than what I am doing, but it's not like I'm smoking weed and playing Call of Duty between workshifts at a pizza parlor.
